name: Bank statement
what_it_is: The bank's own record of every rupee that went in and out of one account during the month.
why_it_matters: It's the only outside proof of your cash. We match your books to it line by line, so the cash and runway on your dashboard are real.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Opening balance (amount); Closing balance (amount); Money in (amount); Money out (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Your bank's net banking → Accounts → Statement → pick the month → download as PDF. One per account.
what_pba_checks: Opening balance matches last month's closing. Every large payment has a bill behind it. Closing balance matches the books to the rupee.
if_late: Nothing can be checked without it — the whole month waits.

name: Sales invoice register
what_it_is: A list of every invoice the company raised in the month — who it went to, how much, and the GST on it.
why_it_matters: Your revenue and your GST bill both start here. If an invoice is missing, revenue is understated and GST can be short-paid.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Invoices raised (number); Total billed (with GST) (amount); GST charged (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Export from Tally (Display → Account books → Sales register) or your billing tool, for the month.
what_pba_checks: Every invoice is in the GSTR-1. Totals match the revenue in the books. No invoice numbers are skipped.
if_late: Revenue and GST can't be worked out, so GSTR-1 (due the 11th) is at risk.

name: Collections received
what_it_is: Money that actually arrived from customers this month — not what was invoiced, what was received.
why_it_matters: Billing isn't cash. This shows how much of what you billed turned into money in the bank.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Amount collected (amount); Clients who paid (number); Largest receipt (amount)
where_it_comes_from: From the bank statement, or your billing tool's payments report. One line per receipt, with the client name.
what_pba_checks: Each receipt is matched to an invoice, so we know who still owes you.
if_late: Money-owed figures and collection days stay out of date.

name: Debtors ageing
what_it_is: Who owes the company money at month end, split by how long it has been due: 0–30, 31–60, 61–90 and over 90 days.
why_it_matters: Money owed for over 90 days is the money least likely to come in. Catching it early protects your cash.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Total owed to you (amount); Of which over 90 days (amount); Largest debtor (text)
where_it_comes_from: Tally → Display → Statements of accounts → Outstandings → Receivables, with ageing.
what_pba_checks: Totals match the books; anything over 90 days is followed up.
if_late: Money-owed on the dashboard can't be updated.

name: Payroll register
what_it_is: The month's salary sheet — each person's gross pay, deductions and what was actually paid.
why_it_matters: Salaries are usually your largest cost. It also drives PF, ESI, professional tax and salary TDS — all of which carry penalties if wrong.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: People paid (number); Gross salary (amount); Net paid (amount); TDS deducted (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Your payroll sheet for the month — gross, deductions and net paid for each person.
what_pba_checks: Net pay matches what left the bank. Salary TDS, PF, ESI and professional tax are worked out from it.
if_late: Salary TDS (due the 7th) and PF (due the 15th) can't be confirmed.

name: Contractor payments
what_it_is: Payments to consultants and contractors who are not on payroll.
why_it_matters: They need TDS deducted and are a common audit question. Keeping them separate from salaries keeps both clean.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Contractors paid (number); Total paid (amount); TDS deducted (amount)
where_it_comes_from: A list of consultants paid this month, with invoice amounts and TDS cut.
what_pba_checks: TDS was cut at the right rate (usually 10%) and deposited.
if_late: TDS on vendors can't be confirmed for the month.

name: Professional tax challan
what_it_is: Proof that professional tax — a small state tax on salaries — was paid.
why_it_matters: It's a state requirement. Late payment brings interest and penalties, and it's checked at audit.
where_it_comes_from: The receipt from the state's professional tax payment site, or from your bank.
what_pba_checks: Amount matches the number of people and the state's slabs.
if_late: Interest and a penalty from the state.

name: Founder remuneration
what_it_is: What each founder is approved to draw as salary, against what they actually drew.
why_it_matters: Investors and auditors look at this closely. Drawing above what's approved needs board or shareholder approval.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Approved for the quarter (amount); Actually drawn (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Board resolution and payroll for the founders.
what_pba_checks: What was drawn is within what was approved.
if_late: Investors and auditors will ask.

name: Amounts paid to partners
what_it_is: What the company paid or owes to revenue-share partners this month.
why_it_matters: If you bill clients the full amount and pay partners a share, this is the gap between your gross and your real revenue.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Total paid to partners (amount); Partners paid (number)
where_it_comes_from: Partner statements or your own working of what's owed under each revenue-share agreement.
what_pba_checks: Matches the agreements on file. Shown separately so both gross and net revenue are on the dashboard.
if_late: Revenue on the dashboard can't be shown net of partner share.

name: Payment gateway settlement report
what_it_is: The payment gateway's report of what it collected for you, what it kept as fees, and what it sent to your bank.
why_it_matters: Gateway fees quietly eat into revenue, and settlements arrive days later. This makes both visible.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Collected through the gateway (amount); Gateway fees (amount); Settled to bank (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Razorpay dashboard → Reports → Settlements → the month → download.
what_pba_checks: What the gateway collected, minus fees, equals what reached the bank.
if_late: Gateway fees and receipts stay unchecked.

name: Advances received
what_it_is: Money customers paid before the work was delivered.
why_it_matters: An advance is not revenue yet — it's owed back as work. Counting it as revenue overstates the month.
where_it_comes_from: From the bank statement and your billing tool.
what_pba_checks: Advances are not counted as revenue until the work is done.
if_late: Revenue may be overstated.

name: Investment statement
what_it_is: The statement for an investment the company holds — a fixed deposit, a fund, or shares.
why_it_matters: It's part of your cash cushion. Interest and gains are income and need to be in the books.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Value at month end (amount); Interest or gain this month (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Bank or fund house statement for the month.
what_pba_checks: Value and interest are in the books.
if_late: Interest income may be missed.

name: Trial balance
what_it_is: A list of every account in the books with its balance at month end. It's the raw list every other report is built from.
why_it_matters: If debits and credits don't match, something is mis-posted — and nothing built on it can be trusted. It's the first thing we check.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Total debits (amount); Total credits (amount); Accounts in the books (number)
where_it_comes_from: Tally → Display → Trial balance → month end → export.
what_pba_checks: Debits equal credits. Every account looks sensible against last month.
if_late: The books can't be closed for the month.

name: Profit and loss
what_it_is: The month's income minus its expenses — whether the company made or lost money on paper.
why_it_matters: It's the headline of the month. It differs from cash (bills raised but not collected count here), which is why we show both.
where_it_comes_from: Tally → Display → Profit and loss → the month.
what_pba_checks: Revenue matches the sales register; expenses match the bills and payroll.
if_late: Profit and loss on the dashboard can't be updated.

name: Balance sheet
what_it_is: What the company owns and owes on the last day of the month.
why_it_matters: It shows whether the company can pay what it owes — cash, receivables and payables, side by side.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Total assets (amount); Total liabilities (amount); Cash and bank (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Tally → Display → Balance sheet → month end.
what_pba_checks: Cash matches the bank statements; what's owed matches the ageing reports.
if_late: Cash and dues can't be confirmed.

name: Purchase register and 2B match
what_it_is: Every bill the company received this month, matched against what suppliers reported to GST (GSTR-2B).
why_it_matters: You can only claim GST credit on bills your suppliers have reported. A mismatch is credit you may lose.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Purchases (amount); Input credit claimed (amount); Not yet in GSTR-2B (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Tally purchase register, matched against GSTR-2B downloaded from the GST portal.
what_pba_checks: Every bill you claim credit on appears in GSTR-2B.
if_late: GST credit may be claimed wrongly or missed.

name: GST working
what_it_is: The calculation of how much GST is owed for the month: GST charged on sales, less GST credit on purchases.
why_it_matters: It's what the GSTR-3B is filed from. Getting it right avoids interest, notices and lost credit.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: GST on sales (amount); Input credit (amount); Net GST payable (amount)
where_it_comes_from: Prepared by the accountant from the sales register and GSTR-2B.
what_pba_checks: GST on sales ties to GSTR-1; credit ties to GSTR-2B; the net is what the GSTR-3B pays.
if_late: GSTR-3B (due the 20th) can't be filed on time.

name: MIS workbook
what_it_is: The month's management report — P&L, balance sheet, cash, customers — in our fixed format.
why_it_matters: This is where your dashboard numbers come from. The portal reads 24 figures straight out of it, so no one retypes anything.
where_it_comes_from: Prepared by the accountant in Prime Bottomline's fixed template, from the closed books.
what_pba_checks: The portal reads 24 figures and runs 5 checks. Prime Bottomline then compares the month with the last one before publishing.
if_late: The month can't be published, so the dashboard keeps showing last month.

name: GSTR-1
what_it_is: The GST return that lists every sale invoice you raised in the period.
why_it_matters: Your customers can only claim GST credit once you file it — late filing delays their credit and hurts the relationship. Late fees apply too.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: ARN (text); Filed on (date); Invoice value reported (amount)
where_it_comes_from: GST portal (gst.gov.in) → Services → Returns → Returns dashboard → pick the period → GSTR-1 → view and download the filed return. The ARN is on the acknowledgement.
what_pba_checks: Invoice values match the sales register. Filed by the 11th.
if_late: ₹50 a day late fee (₹20 if nil), and your clients can't claim their GST credit until you file.

name: GSTR-3B
what_it_is: The monthly GST summary return where the tax is actually paid.
why_it_matters: It's the return that moves money. Late payment costs 18% a year in interest, and missed returns block your e-way bills and refunds.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Tax paid (amount); Challan (CPIN) (text); ARN (text); Filed on (date)
where_it_comes_from: GST portal (gst.gov.in) → Services → Returns → Returns dashboard → pick the period → GSTR-3B → download the filed return. The challan (CPIN) comes from Services → Payments.
what_pba_checks: Tax on sales matches GSTR-1, credit matches GSTR-2B, and cash paid matches the challan and the bank statement.
if_late: 18% a year interest on the cash part, plus ₹50 a day late fee. Credit and e-way bills can get blocked.

name: GST payment (PMT-06 / CMP-08)
what_it_is: GST paid for the month (or quarter) under the QRMP or composition scheme.
why_it_matters: Even when the return is quarterly, the tax is due monthly. Missing it brings interest.
where_it_comes_from: GST portal → Services → Payments → Create challan (PMT-06) → download the paid challan.
what_pba_checks: Amount matches the month's GST working.
if_late: 18% a year interest.

name: TDS payment
what_it_is: Tax the company deducted from salaries and vendor payments, paid to the government.
why_it_matters: The money isn't yours — it's held for the government. Late deposit costs 1.5% a month and is a red flag in due diligence.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Amount paid (amount); Challan number (text); Paid on (date)
where_it_comes_from: Income tax portal (incometax.gov.in) → e-Pay Tax → Challan 281 → download the paid challan with its CIN.
what_pba_checks: Amount matches the TDS cut on salaries, vendors and rent in the books, by section.
if_late: 1.5% a month interest from the date the tax was cut. A red flag in due diligence.

name: TDS return
what_it_is: The quarterly statement telling the tax department whose tax you deducted and how much.
why_it_matters: Employees and vendors can only see their tax credit after you file it. Late filing costs ₹200 a day.
where_it_comes_from: Filed on the TRACES / income tax portal using the quarter's TDS data. The acknowledgement has a token number.
what_pba_checks: Every challan for the quarter is included, against the right people.
if_late: ₹200 a day late fee, and staff and vendors can't see their tax credit.

name: PF / ESI payment
what_it_is: Provident fund or ESI contributions for employees, paid with the monthly return.
why_it_matters: It's employee money held in trust. Delays bring damages and interest and are taken seriously.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Amount paid (amount); Challan / TRRN (text); Paid on (date)
where_it_comes_from: EPFO employer portal → ECR → pay → download the ECR receipt and the TRRN challan.
what_pba_checks: Matches the payroll register for the month.
if_late: Interest and damages; taken seriously by EPFO.

name: Certificate of incorporation
what_it_is: The government's certificate that the company exists, with its name, number (CIN) and date.
why_it_matters: Every bank, investor and government form asks for it. It's the first page of any data room.

name: MOA and AOA
what_it_is: The company's founding rules: what it can do (MOA), and how it's run and who decides what (AOA).
why_it_matters: Investor rights, share classes and board powers live in the AOA. Every round usually changes it.

name: Company PAN
what_it_is: The company's income tax identity number.
why_it_matters: Needed for every bank account, tax filing and investor KYC.

name: TAN
what_it_is: The number the company uses when it deducts tax from salaries and vendor payments.
why_it_matters: Without it, TDS can't be paid or filed.

name: GST registration certificate
what_it_is: The certificate showing a GST number and the address it's registered at.
why_it_matters: Customers ask for it before paying invoices, and it proves where you are registered to sell.

name: Cap table
what_it_is: Who owns what share of the company, including options and anything that converts into shares later.
why_it_matters: It's the first thing an investor asks for. Errors here are expensive to fix after a round.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Founders hold (percent); Investors hold (percent); Option pool (percent)

name: Audited financial statements
what_it_is: The year's accounts, checked and signed by the statutory auditor.
why_it_matters: Banks, investors and the tax department all start from these. Our opening numbers do too.
summary_fields_typed_by_uploader: Revenue for the year (amount); Profit / (loss) (amount); Signed on (date)

name: Opening trial balance
what_it_is: Every account's balance on 1 April — the starting point for this year's books.
why_it_matters: If the starting point is wrong, every month after it is wrong too.

name: Client list
what_it_is: Every client, what they're billed, how often, and since when.
why_it_matters: It's how we know what revenue to expect each month, and spot when a client goes quiet.

name: Revenue-share agreements
what_it_is: Agreements where the company shares revenue with a partner or pays commission.
why_it_matters: They decide whether your real revenue is the full invoice or only your share.

name: Headcount list
what_it_is: Everyone working in the company — role, start date, employee or contractor.
why_it_matters: It decides PF, ESI and professional tax, and is the base for any hiring plan.

name: Debenture certificates
what_it_is: Certificates issued to each debenture holder showing what they hold.
why_it_matters: Proof of the debt. Lenders and auditors ask for them, and they must be issued within six months of allotment.

name: Term sheet
what_it_is: The short, mostly non-binding summary of a deal's key terms before the full agreements.
why_it_matters: Valuation, board seats and investor rights are agreed here. Everything later follows it.

name: SSA / SHA
what_it_is: The binding agreements under which investors bought shares, and how shareholders deal with each other.
why_it_matters: They set what investors can block, what you must report to them, and what happens in a sale.

name: PAS-3 return of allotment
what_it_is: The filing that tells the Registrar of Companies new shares or debentures were issued.
why_it_matters: Until it's filed, the allotment isn't on record. It's due within 15 days and is checked in every due diligence.

name: MGT-14
what_it_is: The filing of important shareholder or board decisions with the Registrar of Companies.
why_it_matters: Some decisions — like issuing shares or borrowing beyond limits — are only valid once filed. Due within 30 days.

name: CHG-4 satisfaction of charge
what_it_is: The filing that records a loan has been repaid and the security released.
why_it_matters: Until it's filed, the company's assets still show as pledged — which can block new loans.

name: Charge registration (CHG-1 / CHG-9)
what_it_is: The filing that records the security given for a loan or debentures.
why_it_matters: Lenders need it registered to be protected. Due within 30 days of creating the charge.

name: Debenture redemption proof
what_it_is: Proof that debenture holders were repaid.
why_it_matters: Closes the debt on record and is needed before the charge can be released.

name: Board resolution
what_it_is: A decision formally taken by the company's board, signed and certified.
why_it_matters: Banks, the Registrar and investors ask for it to prove the decision was properly made.

name: Anything else
what_it_is: A record kept as proof of this event.
why_it_matters: It's what a lawyer, auditor or investor will ask to see in due diligence.
